title: Kaiser-Franz-Josefs-Höhe at the Grossglockner
name: Kaiser-Franz-Josefs-Höhe at the Grossglockner
kurzbeschreibung: The Kaiser-Franz-Josefs-Höhe at 2,369 m on the Großglockner: majestic views of Austria's highest peak, the Pasterzen glacier, and a visitor center.
beschreibung:
Overview

The world-famous Kaiser-Franz-Josefs-Höhe sits at an elevation of 2,369 meters in the heart of the Nationalpark Hohe Tauern along the legendary Großglockner-Hochalpenstraße, right on the border between East Tyrol and Carinthia. Named after Emperor Franz Joseph I, who visited this vantage point in person in 1856, the monumental rock plateau is considered the most spectacular panoramic terrace in the entire Eastern Alps. Visitors stand at eye level with the snow-covered summit of the Großglockner (3,798 m) – Austria's highest mountain – gazing across the mighty glacial landscape of the Pasterzengletscher.

Glacier Experience & Visitor Center

Spanning over 1,000 square meters, the multi-story Besucherzentrum auf der Kaiser-Franz-Josefs-Höhe features cutting-edge exhibitions dedicated to the fascination of ice and glaciers, the alpine history of the Glockner, and Europe's highest automobile exhibition. From the glass-walled observatory Glockner-Kino and the prominent Swarovski observation tower, high-powered telescopes allow visitors to spot wild ibexes, snow-white ptarmigans, and playful alpine marmots dwelling in the rocks surrounding the platform. A secured cliffside walkway leads through the illuminated sound tunnels of the Wasserfall-Galerie up to the Wilhelm-Swarovski-Beobachtungswarte. For those wishing to hike down, the historic glacier funicular descends to the Pasterzen-Gletscherwanderweg trail, where the retreat of the perpetual ice is movingly documented.

Visit & Getting There

The Kaiser-Franz-Josefs-Höhe is accessible daily during the snow-free summer season of the Großglockner-Hochalpenstraße from early May to early November (in winter months the road is closed due to avalanche danger). Access to all exhibitions, observation platforms, and multi-story parking garages is included free of charge in the road toll. Großglockner-Hochalpenstraße toll fee (as of the 2025/2026 season): car day pass approx. €43.00, motorcycle approx. €33.00. Getting there by car: From Lienz via the B107 through Heiligenblut up to the Kaiser-Franz-Josefs-Höhe (covered free parking garage directly at the visitor center). By public transport: During summer, excursion and hiking buses run from Lienz and Kals directly to the panoramic plateau.

Tips

The entire visitor center, parking garages, and large panoramic terraces are barrier-free and fully wheelchair accessible via elevators. Due to the high-alpine altitude of almost 2,400 meters, cool mountain winds are common; warm layers and sun protection are essential even at the height of summer. Keep an eye out for the friendly alpine marmots near the base of the panorama terrace.
